import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between megapixels and price,
# with sensor type as hue and weight_grams as point size.
# This allows us to see how different sensor types perform across megapixels and price,
# and how camera weight correlates with these factors.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(50, 1000),  # Adjust point size range for better visibility
    alpha=0.7,         # Add transparency to handle potential overplotting
    palette='tab10',   # A categorical color palette
    edgecolor='w',     # White edge to distinguish points
    linewidth=0.5      # Line width for the edge
)

# Add a title to the plot for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels: Impact of Sensor Type and Weight', fontsize=16, pad=20)

# Label the axes
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Customize the legend to make it more informative
# Place the legend outside the plot to prevent obscuring data points
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type / Weight (grams)', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels and legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# and how camera weight correlates with these factors.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(50, 1000),  # Adjust point size range for better visibility
    alpha=0.7,         # Add transparency to handle potential overplotting
    palette='tab10',   # A categorical color palette
    edgecolor='w',     # White edge to distinguish points
    linewidth=0.5      # Line width for the edge
)

# Add a title to the plot for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels: Impact of Sensor Type and Weight', fontsize=16, pad=20)

# Label the axes
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)

# Customize the legend to make it more informative
